paragraphs: Black Creek Integrated Systems provides integrated security systems for prisons, jails and detention facilities. It also sells records management software for law enforcement. The company says it was founded in 1978 and has served correctional and public safety agencies nationwide and abroad. It says it was the first to bring touchscreen technology to corrections, in 1989.

Its touchscreen system brings door control, CCTV, intercoms and paging, access control, and utility monitoring together as one console. The design is open architecture, using commercially available components. A licensed mobile device provides physical security management such as locking control and intercom call-ins. Facilities can install NFC tags for officers to scan while walking watch tours. A wellbeing application monitors detainees in detox, with chronic conditions, or on suicide watch. It uses wrist-worn sensors that track heart rate, skin temperature and blood oxygen saturation and detect tampering.

The jail management platform is browser-based and built for county and local jails, handling inmate records, biometrics and analytical reporting. Those jails, the company writes, face a concentration of acute risks including early-phase medical crises, suicide and violence. Record keeping is described as CJIS-compliant data collection and record management.
